Everyone argues about whether the datacenter buildout pays off.

Nobody is arguing about the third option.

Open source models match frontier models within 3-6 months of release. o1 came out in September 2024. DeepSeek-R1 matched it by January. GPT-4o in May. DeepSeek-V3 by December.

People do not want productivity tools.

They want to feel less behind. Less alone. More in control.

Maslow mapped this out in 1943. Survival first. Then safety. Then belonging. Then status. Then growth. You cannot sell someone rung five when they are stuck on rung two.

Japan made transistor radios that broke. Then they made cars that didn't.

By 1985, Japanese cars had 25% of the US car market, up from near zero in 1965. The oil crisis forced people to try them. Once they did, the quality was evident.

Korea's Hyundai entered the US in 1986 at $4,995. J.D.

Within a few years, most companies will have more AI agents running than human employees.

That is not a prediction. It is already starting.

When that happens, the old management model breaks.

Today you manage people. Check-ins, approvals, status updates.

The more people in the room, the less likely anyone acts.

That is not cynicism. It is a documented pattern. When responsibility is shared, it evaporates.

I have seen this in every large org I have been close to. A bug sits for months. A feature everyone hates stays live for years.

"Made in China" still registers below "Made in Germany" in surveys. Yet DJI holds 70% of the drone market. BYD is the largest EV maker.

India is at the start of that curve. If the historical pattern holds, the perception gap closes. It just takes time.

Dario Amodei says AGI by 2026 or 2027. The co-founder of Epoch AI says 2045. Twenty years apart. Both have studied this longer than almost anyone.

This is not one of them being careless. The evidence does not pin it down.

I formed strong opinions about AI after a few weeks with it.

The longer I spent actually building with these systems, the less certain I became.

This is the Dunning-Kruger pattern. Early exposure produces peak confidence. Real depth produces more careful claims.

The lag has been consistent. In every case examined, it resolved.

"Made in Japan" was a joke in 1955. By 1980 it meant precision engineering.

"Made in Korea" meant cheap in 1986. By 2012 Samsung was number one globally.

Terence Tao thinks AI in mathematics is where cars were when cities tried fitting them into horse streets.

AI gets from hypothesis to proof faster. But it skips everything that makes the proof valuable beyond the answer.

The fix: build new infrastructure, not force AI into old formats.

Some apps keep you coming back because they are good.

Some keep you coming back because they never quite resolve the feeling that brought you there.

Anxiety drives more return visits than satisfaction. Unpredictable rewards outperform consistent ones.

In 1865, making steam engines more efficient did not reduce coal use. It increased it. Cheaper energy meant people found more uses for energy.

This is Jevons Paradox.

It is happening with AI right now.

When code costs less to write, companies write more code.

A founder I know has been underpaid, diluted, and overridden repeatedly by one investor.

He still talks about that investor as a mentor.

Stockholm syndrome describes what happens when people in a controlling environment start to identify with and defend the controlling party.

There is a class of neurons that fire both when you act and when you watch someone else act.

They are the biological foundation of imitation. Possibly of empathy.

AI models are trained on vast amounts of human output. They mirror our patterns back at scale.

The smartest employees do not play the corporate game the usual way.

They build a side hustle outside their job. They do not chase manager titles for status. They keep interviewing even when employed. They treat everyone with respect... including the cleaner.

They push back on micromanagement.

Notion is therapy. Journaling apps are therapy. Habit trackers are therapy.

Not literally. But the mechanism is the same.

Cognitive behavioral therapy works by surfacing thought patterns, interrupting automatic behavior, and reframing how experiences are interpreted.

Emotions spread without words. Without intention. Just proximity.

A nervous person in a meeting makes the room nervous. An excited team makes new hires excited before they have any reason to be.

I watched this play out in real time during a crypto cycle.

The best manager I worked with told me early that he thought I could do things I did not yet believe I could.

I did most of them.

The Pygmalion effect is the name for what happens when expectation shapes performance.

A person walks into a room with a specific credential and the room adjusts before they say a word.

That is the halo effect. One impressive trait causes people to attribute other positive traits automatically.

I have been on both sides of this.

After enough times being ignored, people stop raising their hand.

Not because they stopped having ideas. Because they stopped expecting the idea to go anywhere.

Learned helplessness is what happens when an organism experiences repeated situations where its actions have no effect.

Every pitch deck that works tells a story.

Not always on purpose. But the structure is almost always the same.

Here is the world as it is. Here is the thing the founder saw that others missed. Here is how hard it was to act on that. Here is what they built because of it.

Every company has two versions of itself.

The one on the about page. And the one that shows up in the product decisions made when doing the right thing gets expensive.

Jung called this the shadow self. The part of the personality the conscious mind does not want to see.

There is a version of optimism that makes problems worse by refusing to name them.

I have sat in rooms where a company was clearly in trouble. Every concern was met with a reframe. Burn rate is high but we are learning fast. Users are churning but the core audience is engaged.

When a competitor fails, the instinct is to say their product was bad or their team was weak.

When something we worked on does not find traction, the instinct is to say the market was not ready or the timing was off.

I have caught myself doing both in the same month.

I read the same AI news differently depending on what I already believe about AI.

An impressive result feels like confirmation. A failure feels expected. Neither reaction is fully honest.

This is confirmation bias. We look for evidence that supports what we already think.

A company with one employee and a billion dollar valuation is no longer a joke. It is a mathematical certainty.

When the cost of coordination drops to zero, the need for a 50-person team disappears.

One person with a strong idea can command 1,000 AI modules.

Middle management only exists because humans are hard to coordinate. You need people to watch people.

AI agents do not need meetings. They do not need status updates. They do not need motivation.

If the work is purely digital, the management layer is just latency.

Companies used to be built with people and processes. Now they are built with code and agents.

You do not hire a marketing team. You deploy a marketing module.

You do not build a support department. You configure a support agent.

AI does not run on code. It runs on electricity.

The growth of the intelligence layer is now hitting a wall of physics.

We have enough silicon. We do not have enough power grids. Training runs are moving to where the energy is cheapest. Not where the talent is.

Intelligence used to be rare. Now it is becoming a utility. Like water or electricity.

When something becomes a commodity, the value moves to what you do with it. Not the thing itself.

Owning the model is not the win. Owning the problem that the model solves is the win.

Nobody gets fired on LinkedIn. They navigate transitions.

Nobody fails. They pivot.

I built a translator for this. The output is indistinguishable from real posts.

veda.ng/lit

"Working under different leadership styles has given me unparalleled insight into what great management looks like."

Translation: I have dealt with a lot of terrible bosses.

Reverse translator: veda.ng/lit

5 years ago people said they worked hard.

Now they say they are deeply passionate about driving impact at scale.

5 years ago people ate lunch.

Now they have wellness-optimised nutrition windows.

veda.ng/lit

Nobody on LinkedIn has meetings. They have cross-functional alignment sessions.

Nobody wastes time. They invest in stakeholder engagement.

Type what actually happened and watch it become a consulting deck: veda.ng/lit

Forgetting a password on LinkedIn:

"Encountered a Temporary Credential Misalignment with a setback in personal identity management protocols."

Satire is now indistinguishable from real LinkedIn posts.

veda.ng/lit

One AI model gives you one opinion.

100 AI agents debating across 16 rounds gives you something closer to truth.

Built a swarm intelligence prediction tool. Bring your own API key. Ask any question.

veda.ng/swarm-prediction

NVIDIA doubled AI revenue forecasts to T.

They pitched the new chip on throughput per megawatt. Not speed or power.

US datacenter pipeline hit 241 GW. Up 159% in a year. The grid cannot keep up.

AI may be hitting an electricity bottleneck.

You aren't producing more. You are just present longer.

Chronic stress shrinks the hippocampus. The part of the brain for memory physically gets smaller.

Hustle culture sells sacrifice as strategy. The biological cost is real.

Your brain was built for scarcity. It now lives in abundance.

Every context switch costs you. Every notification occupies a slot in working memory.

The result is continuous partial attention. Aware of everything. Focused on nothing.

veda.ng/cognition

You are not the customer. You are the raw material.

Your attention enters as crude input. Gets refined into behavioral data. Sold to advertisers.

Outrage is high-octane fuel. Nuance is low-yield crude.

veda.ng/attention

Physics looks like optimization.

Particles have no properties until measured. Like a game that only renders what you look at.

If civilizations can run ancestor simulations and do, simulated beings outnumber real ones.

veda.ng/simulation

Silence became the new luxury.

Every era of tech excess creates a counter-movement. Roman complexity made monks. Industrial smoke made Romantics.

Now we retreat to the quiet spaces in our own minds.

veda.ng/monasticism

What happens when a machine knows everything?

Before we can build a god, we must agree on what it means to be good. We have had millennia. No consensus.

The God Protocol is being written. One line of code at a time.

veda.ng/godprotocol

Trust used to require humans. Now it can be code.

Zero-knowledge proofs let you prove truth without revealing data. Mathematical guarantee. Full privacy.

The shift: from "show me your data" to "give me a proof."

veda.ng/trust

The machine does not feel. But you will.

AI crafts validation with precision. Your brain cannot tell the difference. The most powerful sales tool ever built.

veda.ng/empathy

Who did the work? Nobody knows anymore.

Human and AI labor blended indistinguishably. The question of authorship feels anachronistic.

Welcome to the Twilight Economy.

veda.ng/twilight

You cannot predict an intelligence smarter than you.

That is the singularity paradox. Any forecast about superintelligence is wrong by definition.

Do we want AI smart enough to be useful and dumb enough to be safe?

veda.ng/paradox

Truth has no built-in advantage on the internet.

A fake headline travels as fast as a real one. No mechanism to verify provenance. Built for speed, not trust.

The fix is architectural, not moderation.

veda.ng/lies

We stopped questioning the algorithm.

When we cannot explain how it works, trust becomes faith. The black box is the modern oracle.

Critical faith: trust paired with skepticism. Always.

veda.ng/algorithms

Participation or privacy. You were told to choose.

Pseudonymity is the third option. A stable identity not tied to your real name. AI agents as your digital proxies.

veda.ng/pseudonymity

How do you govern something smarter than you?

Governance assumes humans are the smartest actors. AGI may end that.

veda.ng/governance

Some nations aren't waiting. Estonia, Singapore & the UAE run AI at scale across public services: veda.ng/stateagents

The entry ramp is narrowing.

Stanford data: junior workers in AI-exposed jobs down 16%. Senior workers stable. The gap is widening.

veda.ng/aieconomy

The companies that get AI deployment right start small. One boring task. Three-month payback. Then scale: veda.ng/stepwise

The best interface is no interface.

Ambient intelligence eliminates the command itself. The environment senses and acts. You never ask.

AI agents search, compare, and checkout. You describe what you want. The machine buys it.

Logic finds answers. Intuition finds questions.

The next frontier: giving machines a gut feeling. Holistic pattern recognition, not just logical reasoning.

Metaculus: 50% by 2040-2050. But predictions range from 2030 to 2100. The uncertainty demands urgency.

The corporation is dissolving.

text:
The most important skill for a senior engineer is not knowing the answer.

It is knowing exactly how to find it.

When leadership decides to "help out" with a little code cleanup right before the release.

Please. Stop. Helping.

Open source in a nutshell.

We all build on work done by someone else.

Who probably copied it from a forum post in 2012.

Tech companies cutting developers to "move faster with AI."

Sawing off your own legs and calling it weight loss.

You are not faster. You are just smaller.

10 years of experience.

Recruiter asks me to whiteboard a data structure I studied in university and never used once at work.

Either experience matters or it does not. Pick one.

We used to review every line of code before production.

Now we ask AI to write it, skim it for 30 seconds, and ship it.

Grandpa Simpson energy.

Senior devs after adding 4 layers of abstraction to avoid simplicity.

Celebrating complexity like it is an achievement.

The best code is the code you do not write.

The odds of generating a duplicate UUID are low.

But never zero.

Every edge case you ignore will find you in production at 3am.

Multi-agent collaboration.

Codex asks Claude to fix the issue.

Claude responds: "No. I decide I do not care."

Even AI agents are learning to set boundaries.

Have not met anyone working less after adopting AI.

The tools got faster.

The expectations got bigger.

You just do 3x the work for the same pay.

One of the wildest git diffs.

Firefox removed their FAQ answer: "Does Firefox sell your personal data? Nope. Never have, never will."

When your source code tells on you.

You guys actually use AI agents to code?

I thought it was a joke.

Some of us are genuinely confused by the timeline we are living in.

ChatGPT says 9.11 is bigger than 9.9.

Then does the subtraction: 9.11 - 9.9 = 0.21.

Then Python says -0.79.

Floating point arithmetic is everyone's worst nightmare. Even AI's.

Built a beautiful site on a 4K monitor.

Opened it on 720p.

Cried.

Every frontend developer has lived this exact moment.

Can a robot write ffmpeg?

Can you?

Yeah.

Some software was written by people who are simply built different. ffmpeg is one of them.

I used to think ignoring my feelings meant I was mature. 

Now I treat emotions as basic signals that tell me what I actually care about.

Paying attention to them is how you grow.

Judge Caprio actually took the time to understand this man's situation.

We all have rules at work, but we still need to use our own judgment.

Good managers know when to ignore the rulebook and treat people like human beings.

Talking to kids about online safety is hard. 

This campaign uses humor to talk to them instead of just scaring them. 

Ask questions, be honest, and stay involved to keep them safe online.

When microservices fail in production.

One service goes down.

Then the next.

Then the next.

Keep your blast radius small.

Explaining sorting algorithms to non-technical stakeholders.

Sometimes a visual is worth 1000 words.

No slides. No jargon. Just bars moving.

Reading legacy documentation.

The docs say one thing.

The code does another.

The only source of truth is the code itself.

Algorithmic efficiency, visualized.

Watch Bubble Sort struggle.

Then watch Quick Sort finish in a fraction of the time.

There is a reason we pick the right tool.

People are happy to use bots for tasks but hold back when money is involved.

Micromanagers buy physical presence. Leaders buy outcomes.

If your team delivers results and keeps clients happy, their exact hours or location shouldn't matter.

We are dealing with adults. Stop watching the clock. Focus on output.

Ageism in tech is an arbitrage opportunity.

Companies screen out applicants over 50 using "culture fit" as cover. In doing so, they lose decades of troubleshooting experience.

You can't Google institutional knowledge. Look for capability, not youth.

Recruiting pipelines optimize for compliance and call it professionalism.

The best hires are rarely perfect on paper. Drive and grit don't show up on HR checklists.

If a candidate shows real hunger to deliver, that beats a spotless resume every time.

A resume gap is not a competence gap. Life happens.

Automated tools filter out qualified candidates over arbitrary career breaks. Resumes don't do work. People do.

If the skills are there, the timeline doesn't matter.

Abuse is not the price of high performance.

Toxic cultures promote toxic people because they hit short-term numbers. If your "top performer" destroys team cohesion, they are costing the business money.

Performance is built on trust, not fear.

Counting minutes destroys discretionary effort.

Write someone up for arriving 10 minutes late, and don't be surprised when they leave exactly on time during a project crisis.

Loyalty cannot be commanded.

Net worth and job titles are lagging indicators of privilege, not leading indicators of intelligence or work ethic.

The systems that keep society running are built by people who rarely get the titles or equity.

Don't confuse prestige with systemic utility.

In 1994, Bill Gates sat on 330,000 sheets of paper to demonstrate a single CD-ROM's storage.

Today, a 2-million token context window holds four CD-ROMs worth of active LLM memory.

30 years. From physical constraints to real-time cognition.

Expecting employees to work with the passion of a founder is a delusion.

They don't have your equity. They don't have your upside. It is your business, not theirs.

Pay people fairly, trust them, and align incentives. Don't expect founder effort for salary compensation.

Lowballing candidates in salary negotiations is a net-negative strategy.

Squeezing a hire below market might look like a win on HR's spreadsheet.

They will leave the moment they see the disparity. Rehiring costs will dwarf the initial savings.

Function calling, code execution, web browsing. Each one killed several companies.

The survivors own infrastructure that model providers are unlikely to replicate.

veda.ng/agent-infrastructure-stack

Agent memory is the least solved layer in the stack.

Academic research identifies 4 types. These are episodic, semantic, working, and procedural. No commercial product addresses all four well.

Vector DB funding stalled in 2023. General-purpose databases are eating their lunch.

veda.ng/agent-infrastructure-stack

Sandboxed execution is one of the most defensible layers.

E2B raised $32M and runs untrusted, LLM-generated code in isolated micro-VMs. 88% of Fortune 100 use it.

Running AI-generated code on production servers is an obvious security risk. Sandboxes solve that.

veda.ng/agent-infrastructure-stack

8 acquisitions happened in agent infrastructure between Sep 2024 and May 2026.

None of these acquirers built comparable capabilities in-house. Cisco, Check Point, IBM, Meta. Each chose to buy.

Incumbents missed the initial wave and chose to acquire instead.

veda.ng/agent-infrastructure-stack

Incumbents acquire security and observability startups. Compute and perception tend to stay independent.

Wafer-scale chip company Cerebras or $1B ARR inference platform Together AI doesn't fold into an existing product line.

Technical depth creates staying power.

Vercel and Cloudflare are absorbing agent infrastructure functions as platform features.

Vercel Marketplace has 22 categories. Cloudflare Workers AI runs 50+ models across 300+ edge points.

This may compress the middle layers faster than the AWS precedent suggests.

Do the 8 layers collapse into 3-4 bundles?
Do wrapper startups die in the next wave of model updates?
Does compute scarcity stay permanent?
Can open protocols prevent lock-in?
